title: Model + config change -> automated schema regression investigation runbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: When model or serving config changes land (model variant swap, quantization profile change, tokenizer update, or batch/kv-cache policy tweak) we occasionally observe silent degradations in structured outputs: missing keys, shifted types, truncated arrays, and semantic field corruption. This ticket defines and implements an automated investigation runbook that is triggered by the existing structured-output integrity sentinel, aiming to localize whether a regression is caused by a model artifact, a config delta, or a routing/fallback behavior. The runbook must produce an actionable triage artifact (HTML/markdown) for on-call and responsible engineers with: per-field delta metrics, example pairs (gold vs current), config-delta fingerprint, Canary cohort weighting, likely root-cause ranking, and suggested rollback or mitigation vectors.
acceptance_criteria: Automatically triggered investigation runs within 10 minutes of a structured-output regression alert
Investigation report contains: per-field precision/recall drift, invalid-type rate, missing-field rate, sample anchor examples (n=10) with model/config metadata, and a top-3 ranked likely root causes
Report links are pushed to the incident Slack channel and to the rollout's trace in the Console (per-route timeline)
Rollout controller can consume the investigation artifact to suggest an automated soft-rollback or temporary fallback policy (config flag to auto-apply must be opt-in)
False positive rate for triggered investigations is below 15% on historical replayed alerts (evaluation dataset)
Add unit/integration tests for config-delta hashing and fieldwise attribution functions and record coverage
Documentation (CONFLUENCE) describing how to read the report and steps to take is published and cross-linked from the Console alert UI
implementation_steps: 1) Define a compact 'config-delta fingerprint' format that includes model id, quantization profile, tokenizer hash, runtime flags, batching policy, and route overrides
2) Extend structured-output sentinel to attach the latest rollout config snapshot when firing alerts

3) Build an investigation runner service that performs: cohort selection, replay of a stratified sample across the previous good model/config and the current candidate, per-field metrics computation, and example pairing
4) Implement root-cause heuristics: config-sensitivity fingerprint matching, field-surprise scoring (entropy + type-change), and tokenization divergence heuristics
5) Generate a human-readable triage artifact (markdown + small JSON) and persist it to the incident store; publish link to Slack and Console

6) Wire a 'suggested mitigation' endpoint consumed by rollout controller (returns suggested action: disable batch, pin previous model, increase canary traffic back to 0%, or add temporary post-processing filter)
7) Create replay-based benchmark to measure false positives and tune thresholds; add to CI evals harness
8) Ship docs and a short runbook for on-call: how to validate report, escalate, and enact suggested mitigations
testing_plan: Add synthetic regression scenarios (tokenizer-off-by-one, quantize-drop, batch-ordering) to the eval harness
Run replay bench against last 180 days of production traces to surface sensitivity and tune thresholds
Smoke test Slack + Console link delivery using staging incident integration
Integration test: rollout controller consumes suggested mitigation and performs a dry-run (no-op) to validate API contract
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Investigation runner produces noisy root-cause ranking when data is sparse; Mitigation: require minimum sample size and fall back to 'insufficient data' with human handoff
Risk: Slack noise from too many investigations; Mitigation: group alerts by rollout id and throttle repetitive reports
Risk: False rollback suggestions; Mitigation: make auto-apply opt-in and require two approvers for automatic reversal on P0 incidents
